style_block: Original concept photograph for a fan game. Subject: an invented 1960s American 'world of tomorrow' nuclear-test show town in the Nevada desert - Googie and streamline-moderne architecture, bleached concrete, mown lawns, saturated accent colours on cream and terracotta stucco. Light: hard high slightly-warm afternoon sun about 60 degrees elevation, intense diffuse blue skylight fill into every shaded face so shadows stay open and blue-tinted and never crush to black, clear cloudless desert sky, hazy dry mountains on the horizon. Camera: full-frame stills lens, realistic neutral exposure, unclipped speculars, readable shadow detail, no cinematic grade.
negative_block: No logos, no brand marks, no readable signage, no real-world trademarks, no game HUD, no watermark, no text overlay, no people's faces, no copyrighted character or weapon designs, no 1950s tract housing, no school buses, no snow, no rain, no night.

light_slots.afternoon: hard high slightly-warm afternoon sun (the fixed condition)
light_slots.lowsun: golden-hour low raking sun, long shadows (variation slot)
light_slots.overcast: high thin overcast, soft shadowless fill (variation slot)
light_slots.interior: interior lit only by window sun patch plus blue skylight bounce

entries.subject: vehicle/coach
entries.saw: Coach front three-quarter at close range: chrome grille bars, round headlamps, cream body, the teal classic saloon beside it.
entries.why: Front-end geometry and the chrome/paint reflection behaviour on a curved cream panel in direct sun.

entries.subject: weapon/hip-idle
entries.saw: Hip-fire pose with a red-dot sight, the weapon filling the lower-right third, street beyond.
entries.why: Viewmodel screen footprint at hip - our rig sits at (0.22,-0.20,-0.45); this is the proportion to match.

entries.subject: exterior/stairs
entries.saw: External stair with an orange-painted handrail against a stone-clad wall, under a deep cantilevered eave.
entries.why: Second access route, with the rail colour and the stone cladding together.

entries.subject: house-white/exterior
entries.saw: Cream ashlar stone wall, a recessed doorway, the pylon sign beyond, a soldier running across bleached paving.
entries.why: Stone-veneer masonry reference. REAL-REFERENCE says we have none of this in the build; this frame is the bar.

entries.subject: map/street-axis
entries.saw: Standing in the road: coach on the left, white house right, kerb line and the mountains closing the axis.
entries.why: The eye-height street read the `streetElevation` station is trying to match.

entries.subject: interior/garage
entries.saw: Garage / utility interior: glowing green display shelving, lockers, a black and white chequerboard floor, a blue tiled plunge bath marked '2', and the car-port door open to the street.
entries.why: Garage access and its interior - directly on the owner's brief, and the emissive shelving is a lighting case we have no equivalent for.

entries.subject: map/street-axis
entries.saw: The Nuketown pylon sign mid-frame with the box truck under it and smoke from a kill; road, kerb and apron all visible.
entries.why: Pins the pylon sign's position relative to the road and the truck.

entries.subject: house-orange/interior-edge
entries.saw: Interior/exterior junction: an orange banded wall, a wall notice board with printed text, floor and a bright doorway.
entries.why: The only good read on interior wall banding and on how bright the doorway blows out relative to the interior - a direct exposure target.

entries.subject: house-orange/exterior
entries.saw: Cream and terracotta stucco, deep eave, glazing band, mountains behind, the lawn and its kerb in the foreground.
entries.why: The most-cited frame in the project's own REAL-REFERENCE.md (25 citations). Already the de-facto bar for wall colour and eave depth.

entries.subject: interior/bedroom
entries.saw: Purple bedroom: lilac patterned floor-length curtains, deep purple shag carpet, a glazed wall looking out to the street.
entries.why: Upper-floor bedroom. The saturated interior palette the build does not have.

entries.subject: house-orange/street-face
entries.saw: Box truck and coach in the turning circle, the far house's street face, the third house beyond the boundary, mountains.
entries.why: Ties the two houses and the third building into one frame - the layout relationship the map was re-proportioned for.

entries.subject: vehicle/trailer
entries.saw: Box trailer flank with an oval logo panel, dual wheels, a carport behind and a red saloon on the drive.
entries.why: Trailer proportions and the carport it parks against; also a good concrete-drive material read.

entries.subject: map/plan
entries.saw: Both gloved hands holding the killstreak tablet; the screen shows the map from directly above with building footprints and player icons.
entries.why: An in-engine top-down plan. Cross-check for `scripts/plan.mjs` output and for the minimap the HUD lane has to draw.

entries.subject: interior/kitchen
entries.saw: Yellow kitchen: upper cabinets, a fridge, a wall telephone, a domed ceiling light, a mannequin in a dress, tiled floor.
entries.why: Kitchen dressing and the interior light level relative to the window.

entries.subject: weapon/ads-fire
entries.saw: Through the scope at an enemy who is firing: a bright cone of muzzle flash off his weapon, dust behind.
entries.why: Muzzle flash seen from the receiving end - shape, colour and how briefly it reads at distance.

entries.subject: weapon/world-model
entries.saw: Two dropped weapons lying flat on pale concrete - a rifle and a carbine seen from above and slightly behind.
entries.why: Near-orthographic top views of weapon world models, plus the red pickup marker treatment.

entries.subject: map/overview
entries.saw: VICTORY screen: box truck and the street from a raised angle, both garage faces, the deep cantilevered eave of the far house, mountains behind.
entries.why: Second, opposing whole-street angle. Confirms the street is SHORT and the house-to-house axis long - the correction made on 2026-09-18.

entries.subject: ui/scoreboard
entries.saw: The end-of-match scoreboard, headed 'Team Deathmatch - Nuketown 2025', with the full two-team table: score, kills, deaths, ratio, assists, ping.
entries.why: Two jobs. It is the scoreboard layout the UI lane has to answer, and it is the frame that PROVES the corpus is Nuketown 2025 - the map name is printed in the game's own header, not inferred from a video title.

entries.subject: interior/lounge
entries.saw: Turquoise lounge: sliding glass door blown out to daylight, turquoise curtains, teal carpet, a coral sofa.
entries.why: Interior-to-exterior exposure ratio through a slider - the hardest lighting case in the map.

entries.subject: interior/stairs
entries.saw: Straight-run internal staircase, pale treads, a half-landing, red-painted wall above, handrail on the left.
entries.why: THE stair reference. Interior topology has never been checked against the real map; this frame sets the run, rise and landing.

entries.subject: interior/stairs
entries.saw: Stair seen from below with a magenta circular wall feature beside it and a doorway through to daylight.
entries.why: Shows how the stair meets the ground-floor plan and where the daylight comes from.

entries.subject: surroundings/plaza
entries.saw: Space-needle tower, hypar petal roofs, plaza paving and the pale city skyline behind.
entries.why: The backdrop the `plaza` station is judged against; sets silhouette scale for everything beyond the fence.

entries.subject: vehicle/coach
entries.saw: Near-orthographic side profile of the cream-and-maroon streamline coach with its window band and painted slogan along the flank.
entries.why: The only clean side profile of the coach. Use for length:height ratio and for the two-tone split line.

entries.subject: weapon/world-pose
entries.saw: A pistol held out at arm's length, near side-on, gloved hands, lawn and fence behind.
entries.why: The cleanest side profile of a weapon in the corpus - grip angle, slide proportion, hand placement for the Duster viewmodel.

entries.subject: weapon/ads-optic
entries.saw: Sniper scope: circular vignette, mil-dot reticle, heavy blur outside the tube, a 'hold to steady' prompt.
entries.why: The ADS optic treatment for the Deadeye - vignette radius, reticle weight, how much of the screen the tube occupies.

entries.subject: exterior/stairs
entries.saw: External steel stair with an intermediate landing climbing to the first floor, under the eave.
entries.why: Answers 'how do you get upstairs from outside' - the owner's explicit question about access.

entries.subject: yard/garden
entries.saw: Rows of white hydroponic troughs planted with lettuce, a cast plaque on a post, the orange slat fence and a curved white building behind.
entries.why: The back-yard produce garden. Visible in the official aerial and absent from our build; a whole prop family nobody has modelled.

entries.subject: yard/court
entries.saw: Painted shuffleboard court on pale concrete, a pierced breeze-block screen wall, timber fence, flag masts in the distance.
entries.why: Ground decals and the breeze-block screen - two materials we do not have.

entries.subject: surroundings/skyline
entries.saw: Pierced breeze-block wall in the near field with a bank of pale mid-rise towers receding into haze behind it.
entries.why: Aerial-perspective falloff: how much contrast and saturation the distant city loses.

entries.subject: exterior/stairs
entries.saw: From under the stair: patio paving, the supporting columns, painted court markings on the ground and the yard beyond.
entries.why: The undercroft the stair creates - a playable space our build may not have.

entries.subject: interior/stairs
entries.saw: Second staircase, terracotta-orange walls, narrower, with a framed picture on the half-landing wall.
entries.why: The other house's stair - proves the two houses do NOT share a stair design.

entries.subject: effect/explosion
entries.saw: A point-blank explosion: the frame is a white and orange bloom with the weapon silhouetted black against it.
entries.why: Explosion exposure and colour ramp at the extreme - how far the bloom is allowed to blow out.

entries.subject: ui/scorestreaks
entries.saw: The full SCORESTREAKS selection grid: every streak icon and name, the cost of the selected one, and the three chosen slots.
entries.why: The owner asked for killstreaks 'in a familiar way'. This is the entire roster and the selection UI in one frame.

entries.subject: map/title
entries.saw: The in-game NUKETOWN 2025 load screen: pylon sign with the atom motif, teal classic car, cream-and-red coach, mannequins, trees, flag masts, space-needle tower, over a dark caption bar.
entries.why: The art department's own composed hero shot of the plaza. Best single reference for the pylon sign, flags and the plaza dressing.

entries.subject: interior/utility
entries.saw: Pale green utility room with a patterned feature wall, a mannequin in a dress, and a doorway straight out to the street.
entries.why: Shows a ground-floor room that is a through-route, not a dead end.

entries.subject: house-white/interior
entries.saw: White interior with a black starburst wall clock, a turquoise glazed opening and pale terrazzo-like floor.
entries.why: Mid-century interior dressing and the fresnel behaviour of the turquoise glazing seen from inside.

entries.subject: yard/fence
entries.saw: A long run of tall vertical timber fence in full sun with the coach roof just visible over it.
entries.why: Fence board width, cap detail and how the sun/shade ratio reads on dry timber.

entries.subject: effect/shell-eject
entries.saw: A brass case tumbling in mid-air with a thrown charge behind it, against a corrugated roller-shutter door.
entries.why: Shell scale against a known object and the tumble attitude - our pool ejects 24 shells and has never been compared to a real one.

entries.subject: weapon/ads-thermal
entries.saw: Green phosphor thermal scope: the world reduced to green luminance with hot targets picked out.
entries.why: A second optic mode. If thermal is ever wanted, this is the whole look in one frame.

entries.subject: map/overview
entries.saw: End-of-round free camera from outside and above the south-west corner: the whole map in one frame with NO viewmodel and NO crosshair - turning circle, coach, red saloon, teal saloon, both houses, the plaza and the mountains.
entries.why: The single best whole-map read in 1371 frames. First comparison for the `aerial` station; the only frame that shows relative building masses without a weapon eating a third of the picture.
